newsitem.title: ITALY: Arrested Italian railway boss to remain in prison.
newsitem.headline: Arrested Italian railway boss to remain in prison.

text.p: An Italian tribunal ruled on Thursday that Lorenzo Necci, the arrested former head of the state railway, must remain in prison under preventive detention.
Necci, arrested on September 15, is being held in the northwest town of La Spezia on suspicion of committing a raft of corruption-related offences.
Necci, 55, was arrested on the orders of La Spezia magistrates investigating an alleged corrupt "super lobby" in state industries and the judiciary.
The affair has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates probe allegations of trial-fixing, illegal arms exports and widespread bribes for state contracts.
Necci's lawyers had sought house arrest or provisional liberty to be granted for their client but the tribunal considering the request rejected it.

It said Necci should remain in jail because of the accusations of conspiracy against him. Other suspected offences, such as corruption and fraud, were held not to warrant preventive detention as Necci had resigned from his post.
"We are happy, it's confirmation of the work we have carried out," said La Spezia magistrate Alberto Cardino.
No charges have so far been laid against Necci or other suspects. Under Italian law, magistrates must submit a request for indictment to an examining judge.
